newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers a bit shorter on US debt - MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers a bit shorter on US debt - MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers took slightly shorter positions in U.S. debt markets last week but maintained a positive overall outlook, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.
"Investors see year-end in sight and may reduce some expsosure, but do not sound negative," said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey.
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark slipped to 107.9 percent in the week ended December 9 from 108.2 percent in the prior week -- its first downtick since October.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 21 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," up from 14 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" fell to 32 percent, down from 35 percent in the week ended December 2.
Forty-seven percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, down from 51 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets rose to 2.35 percent, against 2.11 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 27 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, down from 29 percent the previous week, while 19 percent underweighted it. The remaining 54 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 40 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 9.0 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 40 domestic participants, who manage about $100 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
